item.title: Electric field controlled nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect in two-dimensional time-reversal symmetric systems
item.description:
Here, the authors demonstrate that an applied direct electric field lifts the symmetry constraint on the nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect, enabling this effect in time-reversal symmetric 2D systems with crystallographic symmetries beyond a single mirror symmetry. They propose an alternating temperature gradient, rather than a steady one, as a driving force, allowing experimental detection via second-harmonic measurements. This finding broadens the material platform for quantum-geometry-induced transverse thermoelectric effects and provides an alternative route for thermoelectric energy harvesting. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 245425] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026

Ying-Li Wu, Xiao-Qin Yu
